title: Metric Garden — annotated OKR scratchpad
content:
Metric Garden — annotated OKR scratchpad (Sasha)

Purpose
- Lightweight personal tracker to keep quarterly objectives actionable and small enough to iterate weekly. Use plant metaphors to keep framing simple: seed = hypothesis, grow = experiment, weed = remove noise, harvest = validate outcome.

Quick context
- Quarter goal (Q4-ish carryover): reduce hosted API 95th percentile latency for small chat requests (<=512 tokens) by 18% while keeping per-token cost within -3% of baseline.
- I'm pairing product work (API ergonomics) + two micro-experiments in the runtime team for batching heuristics. This doc mixes OKR thinking + weekly check-ins + quick retros.

Seed metrics (snapshot) — current numbers (week of 2025-02-10)
- 95p latency (small chat): 212ms (baseline 258ms on 2024-10-01)
- Mean token cost (hosted): $0.00126/token (baseline $0.00130)
- Request success rate (p95 errors < 200ms window): 99.85%
- Developer friction score (internal survey n=18): 3.2/5

Greenhouse notes (what I'm tracking actively)
1) Fast-path improvements (prod + experiment):
   - Hypothesis: enabling early-kv-eviction on 4096-byte mem pools reduces tail latency across mixed-length requests.
   - Experiment status: AB test started 2025-01-22 -> 2025-02-11 (rolling).
   - Current observation: tail latency down 12% on treated pool but small bump in p50 on cold starts (+6ms).
   - Action: discuss handshake with platform-engineering to add warm-buffer priming for pools (JIRA-8482).

2) Prompt-level caching pilot for common system prompts:
   - Hypothesis: caching model outputs for canonical system prompts will cut token counts by 6% on high-frequency routes.
   - Notes: prototype returned decent hit rates in internal traffic replay (4.1% overall); need to fold in privacy checklist.
   - Risks: potential stale outputs when system prompt evolves — added version hash to cache key.

Weeding (things to stop / deprioritize)
- Stop manual post-hoc batching experiments that require host-level restarts. Need infra-schedular approach instead.
- Deprioritize UI polish for the rollout-details page until core stats export endpoint is stable (console-and-rollouts team).

Harvest plan (what success looks like)
- Signal 1: 95p latency reduced by >=18% sustained for three consecutive weeks under production traffic shape.
- Signal 2: net per-token cost change within -3% and no increase in error rate.
- Signal 3: internal dev friction <=3.5/5 (target improvement).

Weekly cadence (my check-in template)
- Monday: review last week's metrics, sync with Rohan and runtime on AB progress, decide go/no-go tasks.
- Wednesday: quick async notes to Maya (short bullets), open PR review block.
- Friday: 20m write-up in this doc (what worked, what didn't, top 2 priorities next week).

This week's quick log (2025-02-10)
- Wins: early-kv-eviction rolled to 30% traffic; saw consistent tail improvement. Added cache versioning to avoid stale-system prompt issues.
- Frustrations: infra SRE still needs an SLA mapping for rolling pool restarts, blocked a full rollout.
- Experiment pivots: add warm-buffer priming (small CPU cost) to offset cold p50 bump.

Micro-experiments backlog (short list)
- E1: warm-buffer priming for pools (small CPU budget) — JIRA-8599 — quick A/B on canary hosts.
- E2: prompt prefix caching with TTL and version-hash — prototype -> needs privacy sign-off.
- E3: smart route routing rule that sends <32-token requests to optimized small-seq model variant — idea, need metrics simulation.

Open questions / decisions for manager sync
- Do we commit a small CPU budget increase for warm-buffer priming across Dedicated clusters? Tradeoff: marginal infra cost vs latency gains.
- How conservative should rollback policies be for prompt-cache changes? I'm proposing canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 72 hours with auto-rollback on error rate bump >0.2%.
- Clarify owner for console export endpoint (console-and-rollouts vs instrument-ops).

Personal work-style notes (notes-to-self)
- Keep weekly entries short (3 bullets max) so this doc stays readable.
- Flag hypotheses with [HYP] prefix and experiments with [E#] so filtering is easier when I grep.
- Keep a list of 2-week priorities and one stretch goal.

2-week priorities (next two sprints)
- P1: unblock warm-buffer priming rollout (E1) + validate p95 impact.
- P2: finish prompt-cache privacy checklist and start a 2-week TTL pilot (E2).
- Stretch: simulate routing rules for <32-token optimization and run replay.

Retrospective notes (from last 6 weeks)
- What worked: small, contained experiments rolled faster when I paired directly with a runtime engineer; visibility in the team meeting helped unblock infra faster.
- What didn't: too many parallel hypotheses, dilute measurement — need stricter experiment queue.
- Process change: start a simple experiment register (trello-like) with owner, start date, main metric, roll criteria.

Mini checklist before any rollout
- [ ] Owner + rollback owner assigned
- [ ] Clear metric delta thresholds for rollback/advance
- [ ] Linked runbook (SLO playbook) and contact oncall
- [ ] Privacy impact assessment if caching user/system prompts
- [ ] PRs linked in deployment ticket

Slack / comms snippets to reuse
- "Rolling E1 to 30% — observing 10–13% tail improvement; warm-priming mitigates p50 bump. Will pause if error rate increases >0.2%."
- "Prompt-cache pilot starting tomorrow — TTL 48h, versioned keys. Privacy signoff pending."

Raw ideas (brain dump)
- Maybe add a ‘micro-savings’ metric: dollars saved per 100k tokens for each intervention to communicate to finance (small, actionable number).
- Build a simple dashboard card: p95 + per-token-cost delta + experiment flag. Makes reviews quick.

Next quick write-up schedule
- Friday 2025-02-21: short three-bullet update here and decide whether to expand E1 to 60% or hold.

-- end of doc --

Notes: keep this file as ephemeral scratch. If something is ready for wider sharing, move a cleaned summary to shared_drives/product/hosted-api/notes or create a Confluence page and link it in linked_artifacts.
